title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 152 (Bailee when not liable for loss, etc., of thing bailed)

content.overview: Section 152 provides that the bailee, in the absence of any special contract, is not responsible for the loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed, if he has taken the amount of care of it described in Section 151.
content.glance: Absent a special contract, the bailee who has taken the Section 151 care is not liable for loss, destruction or deterioration.
content.study: The bailee, in the absence of any special contract, is not responsible for the loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed, if he has taken the amount of care of it described in section 151. Current-law framing: compliance with the ordinary-prudence standard shields the bailee unless a special contract imposes higher liability.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: The bailee, in the absence of any special contract, is not responsible for the loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed, if he has taken the amount of care of it described in section 151.

examples.title: Care taken — no liability
examples.body: Bailee takes ordinary prudent care under Section 151 and goods are lost by accident. Absent a special contract, Section 152 shields the bailee.

hypotheticals.question: Bailee took the care required by Section 151. Goods are destroyed by an unavoidable accident. Is he liable?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, in the absence of any special contract, under Section 152.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Compliance with the Section 151 standard of care protects the bailee from liability for loss, destruction or deterioration, absent a special contract.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 152 provides that, in the absence of any special contract, the bailee is not responsible for loss, destruction or deterioration of the thing bailed if he has taken the care required by Section 151. A special contract may impose a higher standard or absolute liability.
examples: Ordinary care taken + accidental loss = no liability (absent special contract).
distinctions: Section 151 is the duty; Section 152 is the consequence of fulfilling that duty.
problemApplication: Confirm the Section 151 care was taken.

shortAnswer: Confirm care under s. 151 and no special contract

keyTakeaways: Bailee who takes Section 151 care is not liable for loss etc., absent a special contract.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-152
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.myth: s-152 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: It operates only as stated in the provision.
